movements.name: Arm circles
movements.cue: Small circles first, then wider. Half forward, half back.
howToDoIt: Stand tall with your arms out to the sides at shoulder height.
Draw small circles, letting them grow as the shoulders loosen.
Spend half the time circling forward and half circling back.
movements.shouldFeel: The shoulders warming and moving more freely as the circles grow.
movements.commonMistake: Starting at full size, or shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears.

movements.name: Cat-cow
movements.cue: On all fours. Round the spine, then arch. Move with your breath.
howToDoIt: Start on hands and knees, hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Exhale and round your spine, tucking the tailbone and letting the head drop.
Inhale and reverse it -- chest forward, tailbone up. Keep moving with the breath.
movements.shouldFeel: The spine moving segment by segment, not just hinging at the low back.
movements.commonMistake: Rushing it, or moving only the low back while the upper back stays flat.

movements.name: Standing pelvic tilt
movements.cue: Tuck the tailbone under, then release. Small range, ribs quiet.
howToDoIt: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your knees soft.
Tuck your tailbone under, flattening the low back slightly.
Release back to neutral. Keep the movement small and the ribs still.
movements.shouldFeel: A small, controlled movement low in the back and around the hips.
movements.commonMistake: Making it big, or moving the ribs and shoulders instead of the pelvis.

movements.name: Standing hip circles
movements.cue: Hands on hips, draw big slow circles. Both directions.
howToDoIt: Stand with your feet a little wider than your hips and your hands on your hips.
Draw a slow circle with the hips, keeping the feet planted and the head fairly still.
Do half the time in each direction.
movements.shouldFeel: The hips travelling through their full range, loosening as the circles continue.
movements.commonMistake: Rushing, or swinging the whole upper body instead of moving at the hips.

movements.name: Ankle circles
movements.cue: Lift one foot, circle the ankle slowly. Both directions, both sides.
howToDoIt: Stand on one leg, holding a wall if you need to, and lift the other foot off the floor.
Circle the ankle slowly through as much range as it has.
Change direction halfway, then swap feet.
movements.shouldFeel: The ankle moving freely. Nothing should pinch at the front of the joint.
movements.commonMistake: Going fast and small. The point is range, and only slow circles find it.
movements.easier: Sit down and rest the ankle across the opposite knee, so balance is not part of it.

movements.name: Front leg swings
movements.cue: Hold a wall. Swing the leg front to back, relaxed, growing range.
howToDoIt: Stand side-on to a wall and rest a hand on it.
Swing the outside leg forward and back, keeping it relaxed and your torso tall.
Let the range grow over the first few swings rather than forcing it, then switch sides.
movements.shouldFeel: The hamstring and the front of the hip loosening as the swing gets longer.
movements.commonMistake: Forcing the height early, or arching the low back to swing the leg higher.

movements.name: Lateral leg swings
movements.cue: Face the wall. Swing the leg across the body and out. Hips square.
howToDoIt: Face the wall with both hands resting on it.
Swing one leg across the front of your body, then out to the side.
Keep both hips facing the wall throughout, then switch legs.
movements.shouldFeel: The inner thigh on the way across, and the outside of the hip on the way out.
movements.commonMistake: Letting the hips rotate to get more range, which takes the work out of the leg you are swinging.

movements.name: Groiners
movements.cue: From a push-up position, step a foot outside the hand. Alternate.
howToDoIt: Start in a push-up position on your hands, body in a straight line.
Step one foot forward and plant it flat on the floor outside the hand on that side.
Return it to the plank position and alternate sides.
movements.shouldFeel: The groin and deep hip of the leg you stepped forward, and the front of the hip of the leg left behind.
movements.commonMistake: Driving the knee under your chest instead of planting the foot outside the hand. That is a mountain climber, which is a different exercise.
movements.easier: Step the foot as far forward as it goes and help it the rest of the way with your hand, or lower the back knee to the floor.

movements.name: World's greatest stretch
movements.cue: Lunge, forearm to the floor inside the foot, then rotate the top arm up.
howToDoIt: Step into a deep lunge and place both hands on the floor.
Drop the inside forearm toward the floor beside your front foot.
Rotate the other arm up toward the ceiling, following your hand with your eyes. Return, then switch sides.
movements.shouldFeel: The front hip and groin, and a rotation through the upper back.
movements.commonMistake: Rushing the rotation before the forearm has settled, so the twist comes from the low back rather than the upper back.
movements.easier: Keep both hands on the floor and skip the rotation, or rest the back knee down.

movements.name: Inchworm
movements.cue: Hinge, walk the hands out to a plank, walk the feet in. Keep legs long.
howToDoIt: Stand tall, hinge at the hips and put your hands on the floor. Bend the knees as much as you need to -- this is a warm-up, not a hamstring stretch.
Walk your hands out until you are in a plank.
Walk your feet toward your hands with the legs as long as you can manage, then stand up.
movements.shouldFeel: The hamstrings on the way in, and a brace through the middle at the plank.
movements.commonMistake: Letting the hips sag at the plank, or bending the knees so much on the walk in that the hamstrings do nothing.
movements.easier: Bend the knees as much as you need to on the way down and on the way in.

movements.name: Kneeling arm drill
movements.cue: Tall kneeling. Drive elbows back, hands cheek to pocket, relaxed hands.
howToDoIt: Kneel tall on both knees with your hips underneath you and your legs still.
Drive one elbow back while the other hand comes forward, keeping both elbows bent.
Let each hand travel from cheek to pocket, hands relaxed, then build the speed up.
movements.shouldFeel: The shoulders working while the torso stays quiet. The legs do nothing at all.
movements.commonMistake: A small pumping motion in front of the torso. The amplitude is the drill -- hand to cheek, hand to pocket. That is the drill's range, not your easy-run range.
movements.easier: Slow it right down and find the full range first. Speed comes after.

movements.name: Acceleration wall drill
movements.cue: Lean into the wall from the ankles. Drive one knee up, punch the foot down.
howToDoIt: Lean into a wall with straight arms and your body in one line from head to heels, leaning from the ankles.
Drive one knee up to hip height.
Punch that foot back down to the floor underneath your hip, then switch legs.
movements.shouldFeel: The lean held by the whole body, and a sharp contact each time the foot strikes.
movements.commonMistake: Bending at the hips so the body folds, which loses the forward lean the drill exists to teach.
movements.easier: Hold the lean without moving your legs, then add one knee drive at a time.

movements.name: Moving claw series
movements.cue: Reach the foot forward, then paw it back under the hip. Quick ground contact.
howToDoIt: Travel forward at an easy jog.
Reach one foot forward -- a comfortable reach, not the furthest you can get it.
Sweep it actively backward before it lands, so it strikes the ground under your hip rather than in front of it.
movements.shouldFeel: The hamstring and glute pulling the foot back just before it lands.
movements.commonMistake: Letting the foot land where you reached it. The backward sweep before contact is the whole drill. Save this one for when you are properly warm, and skip it if a hamstring is sore or recently strained -- this is the position hamstrings tear in.
movements.easier: Do it walking first, exaggerating the backward sweep.

movements.name: Butt kicks
movements.cue: Heels to glutes, knees pointing down, quick light cadence.
howToDoIt: Jog on the spot or travel slowly forward.
Flick each heel up to your glute, keeping the knee pointing down at the floor.
Keep the contacts quick and light rather than reaching for height.
movements.shouldFeel: A quick, light rhythm with the heels flicking close behind you. It should feel bouncy rather than effortful.
movements.commonMistake: Letting the knees swing forward, which turns it into a high-knee run, or landing heavily.
movements.easier: Slow the cadence and take a smaller heel lift.

movements.name: Single-leg butt kick
movements.cue: One leg cycles, the other stays quiet. Stay tall through the hips.
howToDoIt: Jog easily forward.
Flick one heel to the glute repeatedly while the other leg keeps a normal running rhythm.
Stay tall through the hips, then switch to the other side.
movements.shouldFeel: One hamstring doing repeated quick work while the rest of the stride carries on as normal.
movements.commonMistake: Alternating both legs. That is the standard butt kick and a different drill -- here only one leg cycles.
movements.easier: Do it on the spot before adding forward travel.

movements.name: Fast skipping
movements.cue: Skip for height off a stiff ankle. Opposite arm drives with the knee.
howToDoIt: Skip forward, taking two contacts on one foot before switching.
Get the height from a stiff, springy ankle rather than a deep knee bend.
Drive the opposite arm with the lead knee.
movements.shouldFeel: Springy calves and ankles, with the time on the ground feeling short.
movements.commonMistake: Turning it into an A-skip with a big knee lift and a soft, deep bend. The bounce comes from the ankle.
movements.easier: Skip on the spot with a smaller bounce until the rhythm is there.

movements.name: Carioca
movements.cue: Travel sideways, trail leg crossing front then behind. Let the hips rotate.
howToDoIt: Travel sideways with your arms out to the sides for balance.
Cross the trail leg in front of the lead leg, step, then cross it behind.
Let the hips rotate freely with each crossing, and cover the same distance back the other way.
movements.shouldFeel: The hips rotating, and the whole thing smoothing out once the rhythm arrives.
movements.commonMistake: Only crossing in front and shuffling back. Both crossings -- in front and behind -- are the drill.
movements.easier: Walk it slowly until the crossing pattern is automatic.

movements.name: Lateral bound
movements.cue: Push off one leg, land soft on the other, hold a beat before rebounding.
howToDoIt: Stand on one leg, then push sideways off it.
Land on the other leg and absorb the landing softly.
Hold that landing for a beat before pushing back the other way.
movements.shouldFeel: The glute of the landing leg controlling you, then producing the next push. Stop the set if the landings turn loud or heavy, or anything starts to hurt.
movements.commonMistake: Rebounding immediately. The pause is what trains the landing, and the landing is the point.
movements.easier: Shorten the distance and step rather than bound.

movements.name: Alternate leg diagonal bound
movements.cue: Long diagonal bounds, alternating legs. Cover ground, land quietly.
howToDoIt: Push off one leg and travel forward and across, at a diagonal.
Land on the opposite leg, absorbing quietly.
Push straight off into the next bound, alternating legs and driving the opposite arm.
movements.shouldFeel: A long moment of flight, with the glute absorbing each landing. Stop the set if the landings turn loud or heavy, or anything starts to hurt.
movements.commonMistake: Bounding straight out sideways. That is a lateral bound; this one travels forward and across.
movements.easier: Shorten the bounds, then add distance as the landings get quiet.

movements.name: Split jump
movements.cue: Lunge, jump, switch legs in the air, absorb the landing.
howToDoIt: Drop into a lunge with both knees bent.
Jump up and switch your legs in the air.
Land in a lunge on the other side, absorbing softly through both legs.
movements.shouldFeel: Thighs and glutes on take-off, with both legs sharing the landing. Stop the set if the landings turn loud or heavy, or anything starts to hurt.
movements.commonMistake: Landing stiff-legged and loud, or letting the front knee collapse inward as you land.
movements.easier: Step through from one lunge to the other instead of jumping, or reduce the depth.

movements.name: Knee tuck jump
movements.cue: Jump and pull both knees to the chest. Land soft, reset, repeat.
howToDoIt: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Jump and pull both knees toward your chest.
Land softly through the whole foot, stand up, and reset before the next one.
movements.shouldFeel: An explosive jump followed by a quiet, controlled landing. Stop the set if the landings turn loud or heavy, or anything starts to hurt.
movements.commonMistake: Rushing straight into the next jump. Each rep starts from a settled stand.
movements.easier: Jump without the tuck, or tuck the knees to a lower height.

movements.name: Hurdle hops
movements.cue: Hop over low obstacles off both feet. Stiff ankles, minimal ground time.
howToDoIt: Set out a row of at least three low markers -- lines on the ground, a rolled towel, anything that gives way if you clip it. Nothing rigid enough to catch a tired foot.
Hop over them with both feet together, one after another without stopping.
Keep the ankles stiff and the ground contact between hurdles as short as you can.
movements.shouldFeel: Springy ankles, and very little time spent on the floor. Stop the set if the landings turn loud or heavy, or anything starts to hurt.
movements.commonMistake: One hop over one hurdle with a reset in between, or jumping down from a box. It is a continuous row.
movements.easier: Lower the obstacles, or use lines on the ground instead of hurdles.

movements.name: Wall calf stretch
movements.cue: Back leg straight, heel down, hips forward. Hold and breathe.
howToDoIt: Stand facing a wall with your hands on it and one foot well back.
Keep the back leg straight and press the back heel down into the floor.
Ease your hips forward until you feel the stretch, and hold. Then switch sides.
movements.shouldFeel: The thick upper part of the back calf.
movements.commonMistake: Letting the back heel lift, which removes the stretch entirely.
movements.easier: Bring the back foot closer to the wall.

movements.name: Soleus and achilles stretch
movements.cue: Same as the calf stretch but bend the back knee. Lower and deeper.
howToDoIt: Set up as for the wall calf stretch, with the back foot a little closer in.
Keep the heel pressed down and bend the back knee.
Sink down rather than forward, and hold. Then switch sides.
movements.shouldFeel: Lower than the straight-leg version -- down near the achilles and the base of the calf.
movements.commonMistake: Bending the knee but letting the heel come up, which loses the stretch.
movements.easier: Bend the knee less, and bring the foot in closer.

movements.name: Runner's stretch
movements.cue: Deep lunge, hands framing the front foot, sink the back hip down.
howToDoIt: Step into a deep lunge and place both hands on the floor either side of your front foot.
Let the back hip sink toward the floor.
Hold, breathing, then switch sides.
movements.shouldFeel: The front of the back hip, and a stretch deep in the front groin.
movements.commonMistake: Leaving the back hip high, which turns it into a hamstring stretch instead.
movements.easier: Rest the back knee on the floor, and put your hands on a block or a low step.

movements.name: Seated hamstring stretch
movements.cue: Hinge from the hips, not the spine. Chest toward the thigh.
howToDoIt: Sit with one leg straight out in front and the other bent or tucked in.
Hinge forward from the hips with a long spine.
Take your chest toward the thigh, stop where it bites, and hold. Then switch sides.
movements.shouldFeel: Along the back of the straight leg's thigh.
movements.commonMistake: Rounding the back to reach the foot. That drags the pull into the low back and onto the nerve rather than the muscle. If you feel tingling, or a stretch running down into the calf or foot, back off and bend the knee a little.
movements.easier: Sit on a cushion, and let the straight leg bend slightly.

movements.name: Kneeling hip flexor stretch
movements.cue: Half kneeling, tuck the tailbone, then ease the hips forward.
howToDoIt: Kneel on one knee with the other foot flat on the floor in front of you.
Tuck your tailbone under first -- this is what makes the stretch work.
Then ease your hips forward a small way and hold. Switch sides.
movements.shouldFeel: Across the front of the hip on the kneeling side.
movements.commonMistake: Pushing the hips forward without the tuck, which arches the low back and stretches that instead.
movements.easier: Put a folded towel under the knee and shift forward a shorter distance.

movements.name: Standing quad stretch
movements.cue: Heel to glute, knees together, stand tall. Don't arch the low back.
howToDoIt: Stand tall, holding a wall if you need to.
Take one heel to your glute and hold the ankle.
Keep the knees together and the tailbone tucked, then hold. Switch sides.
movements.shouldFeel: The front of the thigh, and a little across the front of the hip.
movements.commonMistake: Letting the knee drift out to the side, or the low back arch. Both take the stretch off the quad.
movements.easier: Loop a strap or a towel around the ankle, or do it lying on your side.

movements.name: Glute and outer hip stretch
movements.cue: Cross the top leg over, hug the knee across the body.
howToDoIt: Sit or lie with one leg crossed over the other.
Draw the top knee across your body toward the opposite shoulder.
Hold where it bites, breathing, then switch sides.
movements.shouldFeel: The outside of the hip and the glute of the crossed leg.
movements.commonMistake: Pulling hard enough to twist the shoulders round, which moves the stretch into the low back.
movements.easier: Pull it a shorter distance across, and keep the bottom leg bent.

movements.name: Lying glute stretch
movements.cue: Ankle over the opposite knee, pull the bottom thigh toward you.
howToDoIt: Lie on your back with both knees bent.
Cross one ankle over the opposite knee to make a figure four.
Reach through and pull the bottom thigh toward your chest. Hold, then switch sides.
movements.shouldFeel: Deep in the glute of the crossed leg.
movements.commonMistake: Pulling on the crossed knee rather than the bottom thigh, which twists that knee instead of stretching the glute.
movements.easier: Do it seated in a chair, leaning gently forward instead of pulling.

movements.name: Lying spinal crossover
movements.cue: On your back, drop one knee across the body. Shoulders stay down.
howToDoIt: Lie on your back with your arms out to the sides.
Bring one knee up and let it fall across your body toward the floor.
Keep both shoulders on the floor and turn your head the other way. Switch sides.
movements.shouldFeel: A gentle twist through the hips and the middle of the back, and a stretch across the outside of the hip. Keep it easy -- this is not a position to push into.
movements.commonMistake: Letting the opposite shoulder lift to get the knee lower. The shoulder staying down is what creates the twist.
movements.easier: Put a cushion under the falling knee so it has less distance to travel.

movements.name: Side-lying groin stretch
movements.cue: Open the top leg and let it settle. Relax rather than force it.
howToDoIt: Lie on your side with the bottom leg bent for support.
Let the top leg open away from the bottom one.
Hold the leg open and breathe -- this one takes effort to hold. Then switch sides.
movements.shouldFeel: The inner thigh of the top leg, working as you hold it open.
movements.commonMistake: Shoving the leg further open with your hand. Let the leg hold itself where it can.
movements.easier: Bend the top knee. That shortens the lever, so the leg is easier to hold up.

movements.name: Knees to chest
movements.cue: Hug both knees in, rock gently side to side.
howToDoIt: Lie on your back and draw both knees toward your chest.
Wrap your arms around them and hold.
Rock gently from side to side.
movements.shouldFeel: The low back opening across its whole width.
movements.commonMistake: Pulling hard enough to lift your head and neck off the floor.

movements.name: Child's pose
movements.cue: Hips to heels, arms long, let the ribs drop and breathe.
howToDoIt: Kneel and sit your hips back toward your heels.
Reach your arms long in front and let your chest sink toward the floor.
Breathe into your back and let the ribs settle.
movements.shouldFeel: The low back and the shoulders lengthening as you breathe.
movements.commonMistake: Holding tension in the shoulders instead of letting the chest sink.
movements.easier: Widen the knees, or put a cushion between your hips and your heels. If the knees complain, use the cushion from the start.

movements.name: Calf roll
movements.cue: Roll slowly, pause on tender spots for a few breaths.
howToDoIt: Sit with the roller under one calf and your hands on the floor behind you.
Roll slowly from the ankle to just below the knee.
When you find a tender spot, stop there and breathe until it eases. Then switch legs.
movements.shouldFeel: Firm pressure -- uncomfortable, but not sharp. If it stings or shoots, or you get pins and needles, come off it and move on.
movements.commonMistake: Rolling fast. Speed feels productive and does very little; the pauses are what work.
movements.easier: Keep the other foot on the floor to carry some of your weight.

movements.name: Hamstring roll
movements.cue: Roll hip to knee. Slow. Stop where it bites and breathe.
howToDoIt: Sit with the roller under one hamstring and your hands behind you for support.
Roll slowly between the hip and a point just above the knee.
Pause on tender spots and breathe until they ease. Then switch legs.
movements.shouldFeel: Firm pressure through the back of the thigh -- uncomfortable, but not sharp. If it stings or shoots, or you get pins and needles, come off it and move on.
movements.commonMistake: Rolling right over the back of the knee. Stay between the hip and just above it.
movements.easier: Put the other foot on the floor to take some weight off the roller.

movements.name: IT band roll
movements.cue: Side-lying on the roller, hip to just above the knee. Never on the knee.
howToDoIt: Lie on your side with the roller under the outside of your thigh.
Support yourself on your forearm, with your top foot on the floor.
Roll slowly between the hip and a point just above the knee, then switch sides.
movements.shouldFeel: Firm pressure down the outside of the thigh -- uncomfortable, but never sharp. If it stings or shoots, or you get pins and needles, come off it and move on.
movements.commonMistake: Grinding the last few inches above the knee. That is exactly where a sore outside-of-knee already hurts, and pressing on it adds to the problem. Spend the time nearer the hip.
movements.easier: Take more weight through the top foot and your forearm, so less of you is on the roller. Or roll the muscle around it -- the side of your backside, the front-outside of the thigh -- rather than the band itself.

movements.name: Glute roll
movements.cue: Sit on the roller, ankle over the opposite knee, hunt for the sore spot.
howToDoIt: Sit on the roller and cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Lean into the crossed side so your weight settles onto that glute.
Move slowly to find the sore spot, then settle on it and breathe for a few breaths. Switch sides.
movements.shouldFeel: Deep in the glute -- a strong, dull ache once you find the spot. If it turns sharp, or anything travels down the leg, come off that spot and move on.
movements.commonMistake: Moving constantly. This one is about finding a single spot and staying on it.
movements.easier: Keep more weight on your hands and your supporting foot.
